extra.message: User-supplied 'filter' GraphQL argument is formatted directly into a raw SQL string via Python '%' formatting inside a sqlalchemy.text() call. The 'pastes(filter:...)' query concatenates user input twice into a SQL WHERE clause without parameterization, allowing classic SQL injection (e.g. filter="' or 1=1--").

The 'systemDebug(arg:...)' resolver passes the user-supplied 'arg' string directly into a shell command via str.format and os.popen. There is no sanitization or allow-listing, so an attacker can inject arbitrary shell metacharacters (e.g. arg='-ef; id') to execute commands on the host.

The 'importPaste' mutation concatenates user-controlled GraphQL arguments (host, port, path, scheme) into a curl command executed via os.popen. The 'strip_dangerous_characters' helper only removes ';' and '&' in hardened mode, but in the default easy mode no sanitization is applied. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (|, backticks, $(), etc.) to execute arbitrary OS commands.

The 'systemDiagnostics' resolver passes the user-supplied 'cmd' GraphQL argument directly to helpers.run_cmd, which invokes os.popen. In easy mode (the default), allowed_cmds() returns True for any input, so the attacker controls the entire command string.

The 'save_file' function used by the 'uploadPaste' mutation concatenates the user-supplied 'filename' GraphQL argument directly with WEB_UPLOADDIR and opens the result for writing. There is no path normalization or sanitization, so values like '../../etc/cron.d/payload' will write attacker-controlled content to arbitrary filesystem locations.

extra.message: Hardcoded Flask SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET_KEY set to the literal string 'dvga'. This allows session/JWT forging and is trivially recoverable from the public source code.

extra.message: UserObject.resolve_password decides whether to return the cleartext password by inspecting info.context.json.get('identity'). The 'identity' field of the request JSON body is fully attacker-controlled; sending any GraphQL request with {"identity":"admin"} causes the resolver to leak the actual password value for every user record.

extra.message: DeletePaste.mutate accepts an arbitrary 'id' and deletes the matching paste without verifying that the caller is the paste owner or is authenticated. Any anonymous client can delete any paste in the system.
EditPaste.mutate updates the title/content of any paste by id with no ownership or authentication check. Any anonymous client can overwrite the content of any paste in the database.
resolve_delete_all_pastes performs a global Paste.query.delete() with no authentication or authorization check, allowing any anonymous client to wipe every paste in the database.

resolve_audits returns the full audit log (every recorded GraphQL operation, the raw query string, and timestamps) to any anonymous client. Sensitive query payloads (including any tokens/passwords that the clean_query regex fails to mask) are exposed.

resolve_read_and_burn returns and immediately deletes any paste with burn=True without checking the caller's identity or that the paste is public. Any anonymous client can read and destroy every burnable paste.

User-controlled paste data (paste.title, paste.content, paste.owner.name, paste.ipAddr, paste.userAgent) received from the WebSocket subscription is interpolated raw into a JavaScript template literal that is then inserted into the DOM via jQuery prependTo. There is no HTML-encoding, so a paste containing <script>...</script> (or on* handlers) executes in the browser of any subscriber viewing the gallery.

User-controlled paste fields (title, content, owner name, ipAddr, userAgent) returned by the 'pastes' query are interpolated unescaped into JavaScript template literals in get_pastes() and then inserted into the public/private galleries via jQuery append. This produces stored XSS: any user creating a paste with a malicious title/content can execute JavaScript in the browser of any other user visiting the galleries.

WEB_DEBUG defaults to True when the WEB_DEBUG environment variable is not set, which causes Flask to run with the Werkzeug debugger enabled (including the interactive PIN-protected console) and to expose detailed tracebacks. This is a known remote code execution vector if the server is internet-exposed.
The 'operator' user is created with the hardcoded weak password 'password123' in plaintext. Combined with the plaintext password storage in the User model, this is a trivially guessable credential.

The 'env' cookie (which controls access to the /graphiql playground) is set with resp.set_cookie(...) and no HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes. It is also trivially client-modifiable (a client can change the cookie value to 'graphiql:enable' to bypass the IGQLProtectionMiddleware in core/middleware.py:122-124).

CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

extra.message: The set_difficulty before_request hook toggles the server-wide security mode (helpers.set_mode) for any request that supplies an X-DVGA-MODE header. An unauthenticated client can downgrade the server to 'easy' (disabling all middleware protections) on every request simply by sending the header, which is a server-side request forgery of state and a security misconfiguration.

extra.message: simulate_load() used by resolve_system_update sleeps in a tight loop up to 500 times (0.1s per iteration) per request. There is no rate limiting on systemUpdate, so an attacker can issue concurrent requests to exhaust CPU and request-handler capacity, leading to a denial of service.

extra.message: The 'importPaste' mutation fetches an arbitrary URL built from user-supplied host/port/path/scheme via curl --insecure. Because the URL is built from client-controlled fields with no allow-list, an attacker can probe internal network services and exfiltrate data (server-side request forgery) and combined with the lack of TLS verification and shell metacharacter injection, escalate to remote code execution.

app.secret_key is assigned os.urandom(24) on line 10 but immediately overwritten on line 14 with the hardcoded literal 'dvga'. The cryptographically random value is never used; instead the predictable 'dvga' secret is what protects Flask sessions and signed cookies.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: resolve_paste for the Subscription returns the global 'global_event' stream of every new Paste (including non-public, non-burn, owner-bound ones) to any subscriber. There is no authentication, ownership check, or visibility filter, so any unauthenticated WebSocket client can eavesdrop on all paste content posted by other users.

extra.message: clean_query() attempts to mask tokens and passwords stored in the audit log with regexes (?<=token:")(.*)(?=") and (?<=password:")(.*)(?="). The lookbehind/lookahead is unanchored and uses greedy matching, so a query like token:"foo" password:"bar" will mask the wrong substring and any password/token not formatted exactly as token:"..." or password:"..." (e.g. PASSWORD, capitalized, or separated by whitespace) is stored in cleartext in the audit table and exposed by the unauthenticated 'audits' query.
